author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read Trend Micro Apex Central security logs in CEF, forwarded as syslog to the data collector over UDP, TCP or TLS. Virus/Malware, Spyware/Grayware and Predictive Machine Learning logs go to Antivirus; Behavior Monitoring, C&C callback, Network Content Inspection, Suspicious File, Virtual Analyzer and Attack Discovery logs go to the third-party alert schema; other log types stay generic.
notes:
Setup:
- In Apex Central go to Administration > Settings > Syslog Settings, turn on syslog forwarding to the data collector (UDP, TCP or TLS) with log format CEF, and pick the security log types.

Field mapping:
- Virus/Malware, Spyware/Grayware and Predictive Machine Learning logs go to Antivirus; Behavior Monitoring, C&C callback, Network Content Inspection, Suspicious File, Virtual Analyzer and Attack Discovery logs go to the third-party alert schema.
- Logon, auditing, intrusion prevention, application control, DLP, update and other log types stay generic.
- Trend's labels in its samples don't always match its tables (CLF_SeverityCode or CLF_ServerityCode, for example), so the csN and cnN values are read by key.
- The CEF header severity is always 3, so alert severity comes from each type's risk field.

Time:
- Logs are sent in batches at the forwarding frequency, so the event time is rt.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples are made up in the layout of Trend's CEF samples for each log type.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-13, and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there.
- On 2026-10-14 each child also passed Run Test in a lab tenant as a separate parser under its parent.
- The engine also stored event_type on the antivirus records, a field its antivirus schema has but the docs' table doesn't list.
- No built-in parser in that tenant matched these lines.

Known gaps:
- Sophos Fusion's Apex Central integration is no longer supported.
